---
title: "Export order settlement for server-side confirmation"
description: "Drop when the pinned release lets a payment adapter settle a transaction outside the confirm-order request."
---

<!-- Generated by `pnpm upstream export` from the patch's commit message on top of Payload v4.0.0-beta.2. Edit the commit, not this page. -->

Only the browser's confirm-order request can turn a payment into an order.
finalizeOrder exists only inside that request, so a customer who pays and
closes the tab before it runs is charged and gets no order. Providers that
report payments to the server, such as Razorpay's webhooks or the mIPS
payment notification, have no way to settle the transaction.

The plugin now exports settleTransaction({ req, transactionID, orderData }).
It takes the cart from the transaction and runs the settlement that
confirm-order runs: the atomic pending to processing claim, then the order,
the cart's purchasedAt, the inventory decrement and the succeeded status. A
caller that loses the claim gets the winner's order back and writes
nothing, so duplicate notifications and a concurrent confirm-order are
harmless. It opens a database transaction when the adapter supports one and
the request has none. confirm-order calls the same code. The plugin records
its resolved collection slugs in config.custom, so settleTransaction uses
the site's slug map, and getEcommerceCollectionSlugs(config) returns it for
other server code. Settlement's writes no longer populate relationships.

Orders get a unique settlementKey, the ID of the transaction that settlement
created them for. The order's link to its transaction lives in a separate
table, so on a database without transactions a request that stops between
the two inserts leaves an order that no query by transaction finds, and a
retry would create a second one. The key is on the order's own row: the
unique index refuses a second order, and recovery code can find the first.

Orders also get a unique cartKey, the ID of the cart they bought. A cart is
bought once, and nothing in the plugin resets purchasedAt, so two payments
for one cart that settle at the same moment can't both create an order: the
second insert fails on the index, settlement returns that transaction to
pending (or rolls back with the database transaction), and throws the
exported CartAlreadyPurchasedError for the adapter to flag the double
payment.

A confirm-order that loses the claim waits 500 ms for the winner's order. On
D1 a webhook's settlement can take longer, and the loser answered 500, so
the browser offered the customer the payment again. When the wait ends with
the transaction still unsettled, confirm-order now answers 409 with
{ status: 'processing' }, and settleTransaction throws the exported
SettlementInProgressError. A 409 is an error to clients that check
response.ok, so none mistakes it for a confirmed order. Confirming again
returns the order once the winner finishes.
